body:
GitHub issue #309. Follow-on to #284 / T62 (PR #304, merged).

## Problem

`checkFlail` returns `{ flail, signals, failedOpen? }`. `failedOpen` marks the
§12 backstop: the detector could not produce a trustworthy verdict, so the gate
declines to cut the build short.

NOTHING READS IT. `scheduler.mjs:74` and `:84` consult `.flail` alone:

```js
if (canRetry() && (await effects.flail({ ticket })).flail) {
  return fail('flail-detector diagnosed a genuine flail — skipping the second strike');
}
```

A repo-wide search finds `failedOpen` only at its construction in gates.mjs and
in test assertions. So at runtime EVERY fail-open is indistinguishable from a
genuine clean verdict:

- the detector is not installed or is unspawnable (spawn error)
- an operational error (exit 1)
- output that will not parse
- a document whose `verdict` we no longer recognize (schema drift)
- `statusDir` is unwritable so no transcript exists (appendLog is best-effort
  by design and swallows the failure)

Each silently reports "this session is fine, keep building". Mistype statusDir,
or run where @adlc/flail-detector fails to resolve, and every ticket in every
run gets a clean flail verdict forever with no log line and no evidence entry.

This is the SAME FAILURE CLASS as #284 — a supervision control that stops
working while reporting normally. #284 fixed why the gate was blind; this is
about noticing when it goes blind again.

## Required behavior

The fail-open POLICY must not change. An unverifiable signal must not cut a
build's normal retry short; the two-strike cap remains the backstop. `flail`
stays `false` and the build still gets its retry. The ONLY change is that the
fail-open becomes observable.

1. `checkFlail`'s fail-open carries a machine-readable `reason`, one of:
   - `spawn-error`         — exec threw without a usable detector verdict
   - `operational-error`   — the detector ran and exited non-zero, not exit 2
   - `unparseable`         — stdout was not JSON
   - `unrecognized-verdict`— parsed, but `verdict` was not 'flail'|'clean',
                             or `signals` was not an array
2. The scheduler emits an operator-visible warning via its injected `log` when a
   consultation fails open, naming the ticket and the reason.
3. A genuine `clean` verdict emits NO warning — no crying wolf on the happy path.
4. The scheduler's effects-contract JSDoc is updated from
   `flail({ticket}) -> { flail }` to the real widened shape.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Each of the four `reason` values is produced by its own branch, covered by a
   unit test per branch. Verify: `node --test packages/fleet/test/`.
2. A fail-open during `advanceTicket` emits a warning through the injected `log`
   naming BOTH the ticket id and the reason. Verify by asserting on captured log
   output, not on the returned object — the point is operator visibility.
3. A genuine clean verdict emits no fail-open warning. Verify by asserting the
   captured log contains no such line.
4. THE POLICY IS UNCHANGED: on a fail-open the ticket still consumes its normal
   retry and is NOT failed early. Assert explicitly, so this can never drift
   into fail-closed — that would let a missing detector kill real work.
5. A genuine flail verdict still short-circuits the second strike exactly as
   before (no regression in the #284 behavior).
6. `node --test packages/fleet/test/*.test.mjs` exits 0.
7. `adlc hollow-test` reports no surviving non-equivalent mutants on the changed
   lines.

## Constraints

- Do NOT change the fail-open policy to fail closed.
- Do NOT change flail-detector; its contract is the frozen rail.
- Preserve `checkFlail`'s exported signature and the `{adlcBin, exec}` options.
- fleet is ESM (.mjs), node:test, no external test deps.
- `scheduler.mjs` already receives an injected `log` (default no-op) — use it
  rather than console.*, so the warning is testable.
title: fleet: make a fail-open flail consultation observable, so the gate cannot go blind silently
